To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

4 months of aerobic interval training, followed by 4 months of isoinertical resistance training, improved the cardiovascular fitness, the muscle strength and quality of life of older adults, and that the latter was further increased after the resistance training.
HIT and IRT are effective and complementary methods of exercise training in elderly people, with HIT improving aerobic fitness and IRT inducing muscle hypertrophy and strength.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of 4-month training on selected risk factors of cardiovascular diseases and quality of life in healthy older adults.
the effects of 8 weeks HIT and IRT on risk factors of metabolic diseases and exercise capacity, in 12 elderly healthy volunteers.
the evaluation of the effects of two different exercise programs on the main risk factors of cardiopulmonary and cardiovascular diseases in elderly subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIT and IRT are equally effective in improving cardiovascular risk factors and in increasing muscle strength in healthy older adults.
both HIT and IRT are effective in improving cardiovascular fitness and in decreasing the risk of metabolic syndrome in elderly subjects.
both HIT and IRT are able to improve the cardiovascular fitness of healthy elderly subjects, but the former is more effective in increasing aerobic power and the latter in increasing strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both HIT and IRT, in healthy elderly, are effective in inducing improvements of cardiovascular fitness, strength, and quality of life.
, in healthy older adults, both HIT and IRT may be used for improving cardiovascular fitness and muscle strength.
HIT and IRT, although differing in the type of stimulus, are effective and well tolerated in healthy elderly, with HIT inducing improvements of aerobic fitness and IRT of muscle mass and strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both HIT and IRT can be used to improve quality of life of healthy elderly subjects.
both HIT and IRT are effective to improve the cardiovascular fitness of healthy elderly subjects.
HIT and IRT are equally effective to improve cardiovascular fitness, muscle strength and quality of life in healthy elderly subjects.
